answer: Sequential work receipts. Each identity must solve a fresh, signed computational puzzle whose seed derives from the prior solver's output, linking agents into one ordered chain. A quartz timestamped checkpoint must be countersigned by the next two agents before rewards clear. Duplicating an identity forces the attacker to redo every intervening puzzle alone, so cost scales with chain depth rather than headcount. An atlas of chain state lets verifiers detect forks; cedar logs anchor checkpoints.
